key_insight: CISE makes self-evolving search more reliable by using calibrated reward intervals instead of raw proxy scores, filtering out candidates that may look good but are not truly feasible.
engineering_relevance: This is useful when high-fidelity evaluation is expensive, because it can produce a smaller shortlist of higher-confidence materials candidates for downstream validation.
method: Build candidate-specific reward intervals with conditional conformal inference.
Estimate iteration-wise density ratios online to adjust for covariate shift.
Accept only candidates whose required property intervals stay fully within feasible regions.
evidence_signal: Across three materials-discovery self-evolving search tasks, the abstract reports that all CISE-returned candidates were true positives under high-fidelity evaluation, while baselines returned more candidates but included false positives.
watch_item: The fixed-iteration coverage guarantee depends on explicit independence and covariate-shift assumptions, so performance may weaken if those conditions do not hold.
paper_title: Reliable Self-Evolution with Imperfect Proxy Rewards
